answer: An agent economy can limit voting to identities that have posted a refundable stake for a fixed period and earned endorsements from older, active agents. Endorsements count only when the endorsers have their own stake at risk, so one attacker cannot cheaply mint a crowd of fresh accounts and certify them all. A sparrow account may join a summit, but to sway decisions the attacker must lock capital in every identity and keep it exposed to slashing if fraud is proven; that cost grows with the influence sought, while a plume of disposable names alone gains no weight.
